prize_parts.citation: for their formal analysis of how special-interest politics shapes trade policy, and for their work on trade, innovation and growth

statement.case_for: B001 remains my first choice after reading the openings. Grossman and Helpman gave the field its canonical formal account of why governments depart from free trade. The protection-for-sale framework turns lobbying and special-interest politics into a tractable equilibrium analysis with testable implications for the structure of protection. It sits alongside their work on trade, innovation and endogenous growth. The influence reaches beyond trade into political economy and public choice, which meets the common criterion of broad, durable impact. Attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist: a sustained two-person partnership, with no large team and no omitted co-originator raised by any colleague in the openings. The work dates from the late 1980s and 1990s and has had decades of extension, teaching and empirical testing, so there is no maturity concern. From my own field I value that it treats policy as the outcome of a mechanism in which interested parties bid for influence. That is a mechanism-design-style insight that generalises beyond trade.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that empirical support for the protection-for-sale predictions is mixed and structural estimates vary, so the case rests more on conceptual and framework influence than on settled quantitative confirmation. A second concern is framing. Helpman is also credited on the firm-heterogeneity candidate B020. If the committee judges that the best trade award is the firm-heterogeneity one, B001 could be crowded out. Trade was also recognised in 2008, although that bears on field balance and not on merit.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B020 first and B001 eighth. He accepts that Grossman-Helpman credit is clear and joint, but notes that the theory has been tested less directly than the heterogeneous-firm models and that Helpman's overlap forces the committee to choose which body of his work is being recognised.
responses.response: I agree that direct empirical confirmation is weaker for B001 and I weigh that in my own reservation. I do not think it should decide the matter. The prize has recognised frameworks whose main contribution was to change how researchers and policymakers reason about a problem, and this framework did. The overlap is a framing choice, not a rivalry between two prizes. His own attribution analysis also points the other way: he identifies a real gap in B020, with the firm-level empirical pioneers (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum) not credited. B001 has no comparable gap. I still regard B020 as a serious alternative and would not oppose it if the committee prefers the firm-heterogeneity framing.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B020 first. He treats Melitz (2003) as the core, points to the absence of a trade prize since 2008, and flags the credit boundary with Bernard, Eaton and Kortum and the dependence of some gains-from-trade results on parametric assumptions.
responses.response: The lapse since 2008 applies equally to B001, so it does not discriminate between the two trade candidates. It speaks to field balance and not to scientific merit. I agree that the empirical footprint of firm heterogeneity on data and estimation is larger than anything B001 can show. The unresolved credit boundary and the parametric dependence of some welfare results make me cautious about whether B020 can support a clean, defensible citation today. I would want that boundary settled before ranking it above B001.

responses.point: Fredriksson ranks B016 first. He sees a coherent research programme in political economics with broad influence, and flags the identification problems in constitutional comparisons and the uncertain credit split between the overlapping Persson-Tabellini and Besley-Persson pairs.
responses.response: I share his view of B016's scientific standing. I ranked it second in my opening and name it as an alternative. I keep it behind B001 for three reasons: the apportioning problem across three names that he identifies, the contested identification in cross-country constitutional comparisons, and thematic adjacency to the 2024 institutions prize. Those points make a sharp citation harder than for B001. I would not treat the number of colleagues who ranked it first as evidence of merit either way.

responses.point: Dreber Almenberg ranks B019 first and B001 second. She values the transparent, heavily scrutinised designs of the China-shock evidence and sees the Grossman-Helpman attribution as clean, with mixed empirical tests that do not undercut the framework's influence.
responses.response: I agree that the B019 designs are transparent and that the core China-shock results have held up. I ranked it seventh because the persistence and magnitude of effects are still debated and because the attribution is contested, between Dorn and Katz and also between the task framework and the trade-shock work. Her reading of B001, that influence does not depend on the empirical tests, matches mine. Our difference is mainly how much weight to put on attribution clarity and unresolved debate over magnitudes.

uncertainties: Whether the committee would frame any recognition of Helpman through B001 or B020. A configuration crediting Helpman under both parts is permitted by the format, but I do not propose it because it credits one laureate twice for overlapping fields.

How much of the novelty in the protection-for-sale framework lies in the application and tractable estimable form, given that the common-agency and menu-auction machinery it uses came from earlier work. This is from my recollection and I have not verified it.
How far mixed empirical validation of the protection-for-sale predictions should weigh against a framework-level contribution.
Whether field balance, given the 2008 trade prize, should matter at all next to the merit of the specific contribution.
I have not independently verified citations or priority claims, and my assessment rests on my recollection and on the colleagues' written openings.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile with respect to B001, B020 or B016. My profile lists no co-authorship or institutional tie to Grossman, Helpman, Melitz, Persson, Tabellini or Besley. I am an SSE affiliate alongside committee colleagues Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg. That is a collegial tie with fellow committee members, not a link to any candidate.
